description: dtp/flow@1 fixtures. For each flow a conforming reducer, starting from an empty book for the organization with the listed ledgers opened in order, MUST reach exactly the expected outcome for every fact in order (an accepted fact advances every ledger it names by one revision and sets each one's head to the fact's digest; a refused or duplicate fact leaves the book unchanged; refusal codes are normative), MUST end at exactly the final book, and MUST project the stated inventory@2 view of the bridged product.

flows.why: a co-packer book: receipts, an atomic multi-ledger transform with yield loss, custody and title transfers, money paid and received with settlements, a signed credit line, an offset, and refusals that leave no trace

facts.why: receive fifty kilograms of peppers, lot P1, at the dock
receive vinegar and jars in one fact: two ledgers, one compare-and-set each
REFUSED invalid: a transform with no output
REFUSED wrong_scope: a transform that does not name every ledger it changes
transform peppers, vinegar and jars into two thousand jars of sauce lot S1, atomically across four ledgers, with two kilograms of pepper lost
REFUSED invalid: a yield loss of something that was not an input
REFUSED invalid: production legs outside a transform
REFUSED revision_conflict: a fact that decided on the ledger before the transform
reserve three hundred jars on the dock for the retailer
REFUSED insufficient_stock: a custody transfer of eighteen hundred jars when three hundred are reserved
release the reservation: the order is shipped below
transfer custody of twelve hundred jars to the carrier's trailer: the location changes, title does not
REFUSED rights_mismatch: a transfer that says title but only moves the goods
REFUSED rights_mismatch: a move that changes the owner
transfer title and custody of one thousand jars to the retailer at its DC in one leg
two hundred jars come back rejected: a status change at the carrier, still the company's
the retailer acknowledged receipt: the thousand jars leave the book to the customer
receive a payment of 6,400 dollars into the operating account, settling part of the invoice
REFUSED rights_mismatch: money received recorded as a move
REFUSED insufficient_stock: paying ten thousand from an account that holds 6,400 and may not go negative
pay the supplier five thousand from the credit line, which may go negative
sweep four thousand from operating to the credit line: a move between the company's own accounts, two ledgers
REFUSED unit_mismatch: dollars counted in euros
an offset with no money: a promotion the company owes nets against the retailer's deduction
REFUSED invalid: an offset of a single claim
REFUSED invalid: a payment settlement with no money in its currency
REFUSED ledger_unavailable: a product with no ledger in this book
a count correction with a reason: two jars broken on the dock
a source that starts at sequence one hundred: a move to the shelf
REFUSED stale_observation: sequence one from a source that has already reached one hundred
DUPLICATE: the first receipt presented again, byte for byte
REFUSED observation_conflict: the same source and sequence with a different fact

flows.why: a serialized product in a second book: units by serial, consignment as a title transfer that leaves the goods in place

facts.why: receive two serialized fermenters
REFUSED serial_conflict: receiving a serial already in the ledger
REFUSED tracking_mismatch: a serialized move without serials
consign one fermenter to a retailer: title passes, it stays on the company's shelf
move the consigned unit and the company's unit to the shelf by serial in one fact
reserve the company's own unit on the shelf: its position is now fully reserved
REFUSED insufficient_stock: shipping the reserved unit without settling its claim
ship the fully reserved unit by serial and release its claim in one fact: the release settles before the leg (#85)
receive two fermenters at the shelf in one fact, one leg naming the shelf and one an exact revision of it: two flow positions that the inventory@2 projection sums into one (#133)
